subject: Inference API bakeoff — summary, quick wins & next experiments
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@cloudmetric.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@cloudmetric.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-21T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Inference API bakeoff — summary, quick wins & next experiments

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we keep the bakeoff tightly scoped and measurable: 

Summary: you asked for a head-to-head across three axes: latency/99th, per-token cost at your typical volumes, and hallucination/regression rates on your core prompt set (billing summaries + support triage). We also agreed to test a noisy short-context scenario (avg. 200 tokens) and a long-context example (2k tokens) for KV/caching behavior.

Proposed quick wins (what we can deliver by EOD Tue):
- Share an initial bakeoff matrix with the exact prompts and metrics (attached: bakeoff_matrix_v1.xlsx).
- Run a micro-benchmark on the short-context set (1000 requests) and return 95/99 latency percentiles + token counts.
- Provide a hallucination checklist and the first pass of regression prompts (attached: hallucination_checklist.md).

Concrete next tests (our recommendation):
1) Deterministic generation baseline (fixed seed) across Redwood hosted model, AWS inference endpoint (competitor A), and a third open endpoint you suggested.
2) Regression suite: 120 prompts split by intent (billing/support/QA) with annotations for expected entity-presence; measure hallucination rate and answer fidelity.
3) Cost/throughput: run steady 50 RPS for 10 minutes using your average payloads to capture batching and KV cache behavior.

Questions for you: can you confirm the three endpoints you want in the bakeoff (we have the AWS endpoint you mentioned; please confirm the third) and whether the procurement team needs an NDA before we start sending samples?

Attaching the initial artifacts. If this scope looks right I propose a quick 30-min sync on Wednesday to lock the schedule.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director of Solutions, Redwood Inference
viv@redwood.com
attachments: bakeoff_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 220KB), hallucination_checklist.md (md, 12KB)

From: Samir Shah <samir@cloudmetric.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@cloudmetric.ai>
Date: 2028-05-21T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference API bakeoff — summary, quick wins & next experiments

Vivek —

Thanks for the crisp recap. This captures what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side before you run anything: 

- Third endpoint: please include HyperscaleAI-infer (api.hyperscale.ai) — that's the one our infra team is most worried about.
- NDA: procurement says we can share non-production prompts without an NDA; full logs will require the standard MSA/NDA. We can give you a sandbox dataset (anonymized) for the regression checks.
- Hallucination metric: can you include both "false entity insertion" and "confident but incorrect statements" as separate columns? Our product folks care about the distinction.

We'll also want cost projection rows normalized to our billing model (tokens + per-request overhead). Ben/Marissa — if you can add a quick per-token delta that would be helpful.

Attaching a small sample of our 30 prompts (sample_prompts.txt) and an initial cost model from procurement.

Samir
Samir Shah
Head of AI Ops, CloudMetric
samir@cloudmetric.ai
attachments: sample_prompts.txt (txt, 4KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@cloudmetric.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@cloudmetric.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference API bakeoff — summary, quick wins & next experiments

Samir / Priya —

Appreciate the clarifications — we'll add HyperscaleAI-infer to the comparison matrix. Per your ask, we'll measure two separate hallucination modes:
- false_entity_insertion: ENTITY appears that shouldn't (binary + count)
- confident_incorrect: model fabricates an assertion that contradicts ground truth (confidence score + note)

Plan for the regression run:
- We'll take your 30 sample prompts + our curated 90 prompts to make a 120-prompt suite. We'll label the expected entity spans for automatic scoring.
- Metrics we'll report: precision/recall for entity spans, hallucination_rate (by mode), BLEU/ROUGE-ish fidelity where applicable, and response token counts.

Timing: we can run the deterministic baseline this week if you confirm endpoints. Full stochastic runs (sampling) and the 50 RPS cost run will happen next week — we expect to deliver a comprehensive PDF with plots by Friday 5/31.

Notes on tooling: Ben is attaching a small harness (token_cost_estimates.csv) that maps token counts to our sample pricing buckets; Rishi will run a KV-cache noise test for the 2k-token context behavior and report latency percentiles.

Scheduling: Vivek — can you pick a 30-min slot Wed (5/24) 10:00–11:30 PT for alignment? Samir — the team prefers 10:30 PT.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
attachments: token_cost_estimates.csv (csv, 6KB), run_harness_v0.tar.gz (gz, 1.2MB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Samir Shah <samir@cloudmetric.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference API bakeoff — summary, quick wins & next experiments

Quick notes from infra/test-harness perspective: 

- I pushed a minimal harness to the shared Drive link (see folder). It supports: fixed-seed runs, sampling-temperature runs, and a steady-RPS driver that preserves your payload mix.
- For cost estimates I'm using Redwood hosted pricing tiers; the CSV attached shows per-token deltas by model size. If CloudMetric wants us to normalize to their billing model we'll add a second column.
- Quantization/throughput note: on GPUs we can enable int8 to reduce cost — but that may slightly change hallucination behavior. Recommend we run int8 as a separate arm in the bakeoff (A: FP16 baseline, B: int8).

I'll start the deterministic short-context baseline tonight and share raw logs to the Drive.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
attachments: token_cost_estimates.csv (csv, 6KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@cloudmetric.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@cloudmetric.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference API bakeoff — summary, quick wins & next experiments

Samir / Priya —

Sounds good. We have everything needed to start except your confirmation on Hyperscale endpoint credentials (can you drop them in the secure Drive or ping procurement?). We'll proceed with the deterministic baselines tonight as Ben noted and aim to have the short-context 95/99 latency + token stats back to you by EOD tomorrow.

Next immediate asks from us:
- procurement: a one-paragraph confirmation that sandbox prompts are allowed to move forward without MSA.
- CloudMetric: please drop the Hyperscale endpoint credentials in the secure Drive link and confirm the time window for the 50 RPS run (we'll target a 30-min window next Wed to match your production throttles).

I'll log this as an action in HubSpot (deal CLDM-4721) and send a calendar invite for Wed 2028-05-24 10:30 PT.

Talk soon,
Vivek
Director of Solutions, Redwood Inference
viv@redwood.com
